standards.name: OASIS ETMF content model standard
standards.abstract: The OASIS ETMF Standard is an ontology/knowledge-graph model for classifying clinical trial content and documents. It was created to provide a structured, extensible, multilingual, machine-readable content classification model for clinical trial content and data and is distributed in RDF/XML (OWL) and other machine formats for use by automated systems. The model was developed with contributions from standards bodies and research organizations and has been used broadly to automate and optimize clinical trial document classification and related processes.

classification.rationale: Source material is descriptive prose about an ontology/knowledgegraph standard (purpose, history, publishers, downloads). The content does not present a field-level metadata table nor an ordered workflow/DAG; it describes the standard and distribution formats in prose, so 'principle' (prose guidance/description) best fits.

principles.principle: Purpose: structured, extensible, multilingual machine-readable classification for clinical trial content
principles.evidence: The OASIS ETMF Standard and its published ontology was created to create a structured, extensible and multilingual machine readable content classification model and ontology for clinical trial content and data.
The OASIS ETMF Standard Model was published in 2016 by OASIS Open, followed by publication of the ontology by NCI EVS and the National Center for Bio Ontology (NCBO).
In 2014 CareLex sponsored and led development of the OASIS ETMF Standard for clinical trial content and data classification.

principles.principle: Based on a knowledge graph standard (RDF/XML) and intended for AI/automation
principles.evidence: Based on a knowledge graph standard known as RDF/XML, the standard, the ETMF model may be used by AI systems for automated content classification, tagging and automation.

Since its publication, the OASIS ETMF Standard has been used by thousands of health science professionals and organizations globally as a tool to automate and optimize manual processes in clinical trial development.
